title: Almond aphids on Almond and Apricot

Header: Almond aphids on Almond and Apricot

Prevention: Collect last year's residues and burn them so that the insect does not stay on them
Use compost and manure to keep the tree healthy and strong against the insect
Continue weeding during the growing season, so that insect cannot stay on them
Cultivate leguminous crops like alfalfa or clover as a cover crop
Keep the orchard clean of weeds and plant residues
Use lime with salt on the base of the tree
Do not grow mustard in areas with almond fields
Pruning during winter when the trees in dormant stage
Monitoring: April, when the weather get warmer; monitor the field twice a week
Look for ant population increase, as they feed on aphids' honeydew
Consider controlling the problem when 10-20 aphids seen on leaves on one tree
Look for symptoms: leaf curl or the presence of small green insects at base of leaf or near veins; check the lower surfaces of leaves
Ask your neighbours to do the same thing, so that you all can control the problem together at the same time
Aphids can turn leaves yellow and shoots to stunt
Use 4 yellow sticky traps per acre to monitor the build up of aphids in field
Direct Control: Spray detergent (5 grams per litre) on the trees
Use winter oil during the dormant season to control remaining aphids
Spray chili garlic and onion solution every week, 3 times to control the aphid
Use strong water spray early in the morning to knock off the aphids.
Plants can also dry quickly and will not get other diseases
Do not use excess nitrogen fertiliser as this makes the plants tasty to aphids
Prune localised aphid populations to control quickly
Do not harm the population of ladybird beetles, as they eat aphids
Restrictions: Use protective clothing when spraying to protect your eyes, mouth and skin
Buy chemicals from a certified dealer and keep them out of the reach of children
Do not eat, drink or smoke during the spray
Use of lime sulphur at 1 litre / 9 litre water
Lime sulphur is slightly hazardous; Class
III; may be harmful if swallowed or absorbed through the skin
Spray in dromant stage of the plant in winter
II moderately hazardous chemical; only spray three times per season, at 10-12 days intervals
